# docs_audit_report — 2026-06-30

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero is genuinely strong — a clear one-sentence pitch, a relatable 47+28
example, and a copy-paste install. But trust erodes fast on the first scroll:
the page states two different licenses, throws three conflicting AUROC numbers
at me before I've finished the hero, and its own blog is mostly stories about
the project catching itself fabricating results. A skeptical stranger keeps the
tab open out of curiosity but leaves unsure whether to believe any number on it.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. License contradicts itself — hero badge + <meta> say "MIT-0", footer says
   "Apache 2.0 License". I cannot tell what I'm legally allowed to do.
2. The first thing under the hero (the "Recent progress" card in the stats bar)
   hits me with THREE AUROCs — 0.9131, "architecture-only 0.8947", "Repinned
   from v2 0.9857" — plus insider words ("repinned", "v2", "dual-condition").
   The headline number contradicts itself before I understand what it measures.
3. The "Evidence" section and the blog actively undermine the numbers: a
   below-random "0.125 FoVer baseline", several suspiciously perfect scores
   (60/60, TP 1.0), and 5 of 7 blog posts titled around the project's own
   system faking/retracting results. On a page selling a verifier, this reads
   as "our numbers can't be trusted."

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- Per-card word counts are actually fine — no bento card exceeds 120 words, no
  result card exceeds 60, the footer is short. Credit where due: the page is
  tight on length. Bloat is NOT a primary problem here.
- Nav bar — 12 links (Get Started, Tutorial, Concepts, API, Problem,
  Capabilities, Results, Quick Start, Report, Paper, Writing, Roadmap). Too
  many top-level choices; a stranger can't tell which one is "start here."
  Suggest trimming to ~5–6.
- Stats bar — 4 vanity stats + a full result card crammed into one flex row.
  "4,425 Experiment runs" and "382 Completed milestones" are internal-process
  metrics a stranger does not care about and that read as navel-gazing.

### Internal jargon
- Stats bar / "Recent progress" card — "Repinned from v2 0.9857",
  "5-seed dual-condition", "architecture-only 0.8947". A stranger has no idea
  what "v2", "repinned", or "dual-condition" mean — it reads like a changelog.
- Stats bar — "FoVer math step-errors" — "FoVer" is never glossed; appears in
  the hero, the evidence section, and the preprint with no definition.
- Features → "Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM" card — "scales Test-Time Compute
  (TTC) based on Process-Reward Energy Model (PREM) variance... intrinsic
  motivation for continuous self-learning." Pure research-abstract jargon;
  tells a user nothing about what it does for them.
- Features → "APIs & portable memory" — `VerdictRecord`, `SessionMemory`,
  "candidate-level reranking", "MCP server" with no gloss.
- Results card tags — "EstimationVerifier SVAMP AUC", "VeriCoT", "CRANE",
  "HalluGuard v3", "CCTU", "PRM-BiasBench-style", "k=5 ensemble",
  "Ising-guided fuzzing", "publication gate". This is a wall of unexplained
  benchmark/internal names; a stranger can't parse a single tag with confidence.
- Preprint — "paper-v6", "non-operator environment", "operator-initiated
  upload". "v6" and "operator" are internal vocabulary.

### Per-milestone narrative
- No raw ".NNN / 2026.MM.NNN" milestone strings made it into prose (good — this
  is cleaner than the brief's worst-case). The closest offenders are the
  versioned/internal labels noted above ("v2 0.9857", "HalluGuard v3",
  "paper-v6"), which carry the same "internal status report" smell without
  being literal milestone numbers.

### Inconsistencies
- LICENSE: "MIT-0" (hero badge, line 291; <meta description>, line 7) vs
  "Apache 2.0 License" (footer, line 766). Direct contradiction on a legally
  material fact.
- AUROC for FoVer: hero stat says 0.9131; the adjacent card says 0.9131 AND
  0.8947 AND a retracted 0.9857. Three numbers, one headline.
- "FoVer" used two incompatible ways: hero/preprint headline it at 0.9131
  AUROC (good); the math-reasoning result card calls "0.125 FoVer baseline" —
  so on the same page FoVer is both the strong result and a near-broken
  baseline, with nothing telling the stranger these are different things.
- The arithmetic example drifts: hero and problem intro use "47 + 28 = 76";
  the "One-word-at-a-time" card uses "47 + 28 = 7". Same example, two different
  wrong answers, side by side.
- HumanEval pass-rate appears three times with three deltas and baselines:
  "+3.0 points" (code card), "66%→84% (+18pp)" (Ising fuzzing), "70%→85%
  (+15pp)" (CRANE). A stranger can't tell which is "the" code result, and the
  capabilities section headlines the weakest one (+3).
- Section framing mismatch: heading "Seven capabilities" under the label "What
  you can check," but 3 of the 7 cards (Research operations, APIs & portable
  memory, TTC & PREM) are not things you check — they're internal process /
  integration surfaces.
- Results intro promises "synthetic-pilot... rows are labeled by provenance" and
  "included only when the card says so" — but no card is labeled a synthetic
  pilot. Either the disclaimer is unnecessary noise or the labeling is missing.

### Missing essentials
- WHO maintains it: only a name in the footer copyright ("Ian Blenke"). No
  About/team/affiliation. A stranger can't tell if this is one person's side
  project or a backed lab — material to a trust decision.
- WHY trust the numbers: partially answered (checked-in artifacts, one
  independent reproduction) but actively undercut by the issues above.
- License: present but contradictory (see Inconsistencies) — effectively
  missing a trustworthy answer.
- What it DOES / how to install: both well covered (the page's strengths).

### Fabrication signals
- "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" (100% on n=60, no false-positive rate).
- "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" (perfect 1.0, TP-only, no FP anchor).
- "99.3% of wrong code flagged" (code card) — very high recall with no
  precision/FPR; an all-flag classifier also "flags" 100% of wrong code.
- "0.125 FoVer baseline" — an AUC below 0.5 is worse-than-random; presented as
  the foil that makes "0.90 AUC" look enormous. Reads as misleading or broken.
- "0.0pp accuracy delta with 4.4% cost savings" (Cascade routing) — headlining
  "no accuracy change" as a result card looks like padding the evidence grid.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero is excellent: one-sentence "checks whether an answer is internally
  consistent — and suggests a fix," a concrete 47+28 hook, and `pip install
  carnot-ebm` visible immediately.
- The "Extract → Check → Repair" explanation and the 5-line quickstart are
  clear, honest, and consistent with the hero example (correct: 75).
- Per-card length discipline is good — the page is not a wall of text.

## RECOMMENDED OPERATOR ACTIONS
1. Fix the license contradiction first — pick one (MIT-0 or Apache 2.0) and make
   the hero badge, <meta description>, and footer agree.
2. Collapse the hero "Recent progress" card to ONE headline AUROC with a plain
   gloss (e.g. "0.91 AUROC catching math reasoning errors"); move "repinned/v2/
   two-AUROCs" nuance to the blog post that already exists.
3. Cut or rewrite the "0.125 FoVer baseline" card; never present a below-random
   baseline as a foil. Add a false-positive/precision anchor next to every
   perfect-looking score (60/60, TP 1.0, 99.3%) or drop those cards.
4. Reconsider the blog selection on the front page — 5 of 7 posts are about the
   project's own fabrications/retractions. Keep one (it signals integrity), lead
   instead with capability/how-it-works posts.
5. Rewrite or remove the "TTC & PREM" card and de-jargon the result-card tags
   (expand or footnote SVAMP, VeriCoT, CRANE, CCTU, PRM-BiasBench, FoVer).
6. Replace the "382 milestones / 4,425 runs" vanity stats with user-relevant
   numbers; add a one-line "Who builds this" so the maintainer/affiliation is
   visible.
7. Make the arithmetic example consistent ("= 76" everywhere) and pick a single
   canonical HumanEval result to headline.
